title: Ramsey, the dancer who fronted Hayes's band
summary: Goodwin explains the band hired a Chicago dancer, Ramsey, as a flashy front man and paid him from their own pay, making 13 men on a 12-man contract.

bands.name: Andy Kirk and His Clouds of Joy

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Well, I know that we talked about Thamon Hayes. As a matter of fact, we talked about Thamon Hayes yesterday so we don't have to go into the unfortunate experiences that the band suffered; however, I would like to
the whole band was fined for working under scale.
Oh, I never heard about that before.
Uh-huh, the reason -- the reason that we were working under scale, the band was hired for 12 pieces. We had picked up Ramsey, a guy by the name of Ramsey was a dancer to front our band. It was a --
Excuse me, Crook. Was that his last name or his first name?
His last name was Ramsey. I can't remember his first name.
And why would he front the band rather than --
Well because --
Thamon?
Ramon?
-- he could dance. We wanted an act in front of the band sort of.
When you say front the band, you mean an act with the band but not really to stomp off the numbers?
No, he didn't stomp off the numbers but he faked as being a director.
Oh, I see.

See, it was popular during that time, the guys -- they weren't actually directors as such but they would get in front of the band and it looked good, you know. Most of them could dance a little bit and it gave a flash to

the band, you know, gave a sort of personality like thing to the band and this was the going thing. Every big band Bus Moten practically -- Bus Moten was fronting Benny's band and playing accordion and there was a fellow from Oklahoma -- I can't think of his name, his name slips me now -- but he was fronting Andy Kirk's band. Every big band had a musical director, such as he was, in front of it. They weren't really music directors but they were guys that could add flash and could dance and this was the big going thing. So we didn't want to be different so we got one.
You got this fellow named Ramsey. Then what happened?
That was a sorry day because we were taking money from each individual in the band to pay his salary.
But your contract called for 12 men and there were 13.
Right. He turned us into the union.
Ramsey did?

Ramsey turned us in and this is gratitude for you. He turned us in to the union and said we were not making enough money but the reason we weren't making enough money because we were taking money from our money to pay his salary.
